title: Saturation of the Three Unresolved Four-Visible-Node Marginalized DAG Models
banked_reason: Delivered tier subfield below floor field; not salvageable within scope.
gap_reasons: The narrow high-cardinality resolution, absence of an applied consequence, and incomplete exhaustive priority clearance constrain the leading-econometrics-journal score despite the substantive open-case result.
It does not settle binary saturation, characterize the models, or establish global witness minimality.

No faithful same-topic in-scope repair can reach field without a major new result outside delivered scope: binary saturation, model characterization, global witness/cardinality minimality, or a genuine applied consequence.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved the unrestricted-model response-and-entropy inequality, an explicit full-support rational violation at cardinalities (17,2,5,5), and incompatibility transfer to all three exceptional mDAGs; both typed D0.5 panels passed after the Fraser finite-reduction scope was repaired and source-attested. The cold tier referee nevertheless capped the sound package at subfield (7.2 versus the 7.4 field threshold). Reaching field would require a new program on binary saturation, full model characterization, global witness minimality, or a genuine application.
tldr: The three exceptional four-visible-node mDAGs are nonsaturated by a probability-sensitive obstruction even though the relevant switching support is realizable. For the corrected graph (g), every law in the unrestricted observable model \(M_g\) is first put into the finite independent-source normal form by an explicit canonical exo-simplicial reduction using Fraser2020, Appendix B.1, Lemma 8 and Appendix B.2, Theorem 9. The response-consistency argument then yields a noise- and imbalance-tolerant observable entropy inequality, and a strictly positive rational law on \((17,2,5,5)\) violates it; verified model inclusions transfer incompatibility to graphs (e) and (f). No global cardinality minimality, binary nonsaturation, or equality of support families is claimed.
gap: The 2024 classification and the September 2026 version of the observational-partial-order paper both leave exactly these three four-visible-node cases unresolved. Existing support checks cannot settle a distribution-level obstruction on a realizable support, and the reported ordinary projected-Shannon calculation did not separate the cases.
fill: Prove the explicit normal-form representation, the realization-level robust three-response lemma, the averaging/decoder bridge that eliminates the chosen realization, the p-only observable inequality, the exact rational violation, and the downward model inclusions. Establish the permutation-support simulator and the fair q=4 SCM as controls showing respectively that the obstruction concerns weights rather than support and that the exact numerical threshold is attained.
